newsitem.title: USA: Boeing CEO says Clinton did not lean on him.
newsitem.headline: Boeing CEO says Clinton did not lean on him.

text.p: Boeing chief executive officer Phil Condit said Wednesday neither President Clinton nor others in the administration asked Boeing and McDonnell Douglas to make concessions to the European Union in order to avoid a trade war.

"No," he said, answering a question at a news conference about the compromise the companies reached with the EU. "We were in contact with the administration on a continuous basis to make sure that they were apprised of where we were but the negotiation was ours."
The agreement with the EU came only hours before the European Commission was to vote on the deal. Until final negotiations began Tuesday, the EC was poised to vote against the deal.
Condit said that under the agreement with the EU the Douglas division of McDonnell Douglas would be a separate legal entity, but would be managed jointly with the other parts of Boeing.

Boeing also agreed to release Continental, Delta and American airlines from controversial long-term exclusive supplier agreements, but Condit said that Boeing would continue to honor the low prices it had negotiated in return for those exclusive pacts.
Nonetheless, Condit said he was confident that the concessions would not affect the long-term profitablity of the combined company.
"I believe that, given this agreement, we can have -- if not zero impact -- minimal impact on the bottom line," he said.
Condit also held out the possibility that Boeing may use a commercial product from Douglas -- the MD95 -- as the basis for a derivative airliner seating fewer than 100 passengers.
One concern raised by the EU was that the American airplane manufacturers were getting new technology and know-how, learned as they carried out large defense contracts with the government.
The new Boeing will license some of that technology to the European airplane consortium, Airbus Industrie.

Limits on direct and indirect government subsidies to the commercial airline industry were dealt with in a 1992 agreement between the EU and the United States. Condit said no changes in the agreement were required for Boeing to share its technology with Airbus.
McDonnell Douglas chief executive officer Harry Stonecipher said that shareholders meetings would be held Friday, and the two companies would merge early next month.
